context:
Follow the CloudSpecs reference architecture: Vite build + DuckDB-WASM for
browser-side analytics. Keep the framework minimal - Preact or vanilla TS.
Pre-render known routes at build time for SEO; use client-side routing only
for dynamic views (compare).
description:
Set up the frontend project for the results explorer at `benchbox.dev/results/`.
The explorer is a standalone static app built with Vite and TypeScript that
uses DuckDB-WASM for browser-side analytics over the derived read model.

This TODO covers project scaffolding, build configuration, DuckDB-WASM
integration, data loading layer, and the shared layout/navigation shell.
Individual pages (home, browse, detail, compare) are separate TODOs.

Technology stack:
- Build: Vite 6+
- Language: TypeScript (strict mode)
- Framework: Preact (lightweight) or vanilla TS - decide in w1
- Analytics: DuckDB-WASM (@duckdb/duckdb-wasm)
- Styling: Tailwind CSS or minimal custom CSS
- Routing: File-based real paths (not hash routing) for stable share URLs

The app builds into `results-explorer/dist/`; the GitHub Pages workflow then
copies that output into `site/results/` so it deploys alongside the existing
landing page, docs, and blog.

**Dependency note:** `resolve-results-explorer-brand-ownership` is NOT a
blocker for scaffolding - implementation proceeds with BenchBox placement as
the working default. Brand must be resolved before launch (tracked in
`launch-results-explorer-acceptance-and-seed`).

`build-static-pipeline-bundles-to-read-model` is NOT a blocker for the
scaffold shell (layout, routing, DuckDB-WASM init). The data access layer
(w2) uses fixture data during development; production read models are
injected by the pipeline at CI time. Page-level TODOs
(`implement-explorer-home-and-browse-pages`, `implement-results-compare-view`)
carry the explicit pipeline dependency so the scaffold can start as soon as
the strategy is complete.

anti_patterns.instead: load it lazily on first analytics interaction

anti_patterns.dont: couple the explorer build to the Sphinx docs build
anti_patterns.instead: build independently and assemble in CI
anti_patterns.why: they have different toolchains and lifecycles

anti_patterns.instead: use real paths with GitHub Pages 404 fallback
anti_patterns.why: benchmark result URLs must be stable and shareable

preserves.behavior: Explorer URLs must be real paths (not hash-based) for stable sharing and SEO
The existing benchbox.dev landing page, docs, and blog must continue to build and deploy independently

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && npm run build && ls dist/
verifications.description: Vite build succeeds and produces correct output
DuckDB-WASM loads and queries work in local preview
verifications.expected: Server running, explorer pages accessible at localhost:3000/results/

work_units.notes:
Decide: Preact (JSX component model, ~3KB) vs vanilla TypeScript (no framework).
Recommendation: start with Preact - the component model helps for interactive
views (compare, filters) without the weight of React.

Initialize the project at `results-explorer/` (or `site/results/`):
- `npm create vite@latest results-explorer -- --template preact-ts`
- Configure `vite.config.ts` with `base: '/results/'` for GitHub Pages subpath
- Add TypeScript strict mode
- Add `.gitignore` for node_modules, dist/
work_units.summary: Choose component model and initialize Vite project

work_units.notes:
Install `@duckdb/duckdb-wasm` and create a data access module that:
1. Initializes DuckDB-WASM on first use (lazy loading)
2. Fetches and registers `results.duckdb` from the static data directory
3. Exposes typed query functions:
   - `getManifest()` - fetch and parse `manifest.json`
   - `queryResults(filters)` - SQL query against DuckDB for filtered results
   - `queryQueries(resultId)` - get query timings for a specific result
   - `compareResults(ids[])` - get side-by-side query data for comparison
4. Handles loading states and errors gracefully

DuckDB-WASM WASM files should be served from the same origin (copy to
`public/` or configure CDN). Test that the .duckdb file loads correctly
in Chrome, Firefox, and Safari.
work_units.summary: Integrate DuckDB-WASM and build the data access layer

work_units.notes:
Create the shared layout that wraps all explorer pages:
- Header with BenchBox logo/name and nav links (Home, Docs, Blog, Results)
- Results-specific sub-navigation (Browse by Benchmark, Browse by Platform)
- Footer consistent with the rest of benchbox.dev
- Responsive layout (desktop + tablet + mobile)

The header should match the existing benchbox.dev site navigation so the
explorer feels integrated, not like a separate app. Read the existing
landing page header for visual consistency.
work_units.summary: Build shared layout shell with navigation, header, and footer

work_units.notes:
Set up routing that produces real URL paths (not hash-based):
- `/results/` - home
- `/results/tpch/` - benchmark index
- `/results/duckdb/` - platform index
- `/results/r/{result_id}` - result detail
- `/results/compare?ids=id1,id2` - compare view

For GitHub Pages (no server-side routing), use one of:
a) Pre-render all known routes at build time (preferred - enables SEO)
b) 404.html fallback that handles client-side routing
c) Both: pre-render known routes + fallback for dynamic paths

Recommendation: pre-render browse and detail pages at build time using
manifest.json. Compare view uses query params and client-side rendering.
work_units.summary: Configure routing for real URL paths

work_units.notes:
Configure the full build pipeline:
1. `npm run build` produces optimized output in `dist/`
2. Verify `base: '/results/'` produces correct asset paths
3. Verify DuckDB-WASM files are included in the output
4. Verify static data files (manifest.json, details/, results.duckdb) are
   copied to `dist/data/`
5. Test locally with `npx serve dist` that all routes work
6. Document build prerequisites in a README
work_units.summary: Add build scripts and verify Vite output
